# Semble answers wrongly from top to bottom — diagnose it without a test suite

This tool reads a folder of code, cuts each document into pieces, records those pieces so that later someone can ask which parts of the project relate to a phrase they type, and answers such questions from a terminal, from a background service an assistant talks to, and from a library. Every one of those paths now answers wrongly. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Below is everything we managed to observe from the outside, arranged by what we were doing at the time rather than by where we guessed the trouble lives.

Preparing a project for later questions mislabels everything it produces: each recorded piece carries the document's text where its path belongs and the path where its text belongs, so restricting the work to source alone no longer keeps markdown out, asking for documentation no longer pulls markdown in, and working over a cloned repository can show neither a piece whose path ends in the name we committed nor paths that stay relative to the repository root. Gathering the contents of a directory tree honours plain exclusion rules but mishandles any exclusion list containing a negation: after a blanket exclusion, a rule re-admitting a directory's contents does not take effect, and a rule re-admitting things under a dotted directory produces a different set than the rules describe.
